svg.text: FIGURE 2: CANONICAL RLC ELEMENTS & DEPENDENT SOURCES ARCHITECTURE
Passive R, L, C Physics, Duality Pairs, State Variable Continuity, and the 4 Controlled Source Topologies

g.text: 1. Ideal Resistor & Ohm's Law Dynamics
Constitutive V-I Relation & Dissipation
• Ohm's Law in Linear Resistors: v(t) = R · i(t) ⟺ i(t) = G · v(t)
Conductance G = 1/R [Siemens / ℧]
• Strictly Dissipative / Passive: Instantaneous power p(t) ≥ 0:
p(t) = v(t) · i(t) = i²(t) R = v²(t) / R ≥ 0
• Energy dissipated is converted permanently into thermal heat (Joulean loss).
• Resistor has ZERO energy storage capability: w_R = 0 J.
Physical Sizing & Temperature Dynamics
• Microscopic Geometry: R = ρ · (l / A) = (1 / σ) · (l / A)
ρ = resistivity (Ω·m), σ = conductivity (S/m), l = length, A = area.
Thermal Resistance Equation:
R(T) = R₀ [ 1 + α (T - T₀) ]
• Metals / Conductors: α > 0 (PTC: resistance increases with heating).
• Semiconductors / Insulators: α < 0 (NTC: resistance falls with heating).
• Manganin / Constantan: α ≈ 0 (Used for standard precision meter shunts!).
Series / Parallel & Divider Rules
Series Resistors (Common Current):
R_eq = R₁ + R₂ + ... + R_n
• Voltage Divider Rule (VDR):
V_k = V_s · [ R_k / (R₁ + R₂ + ... + R_n) ]
Parallel Resistors (Common Voltage):
1/R_eq = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + ... ⟺ G_eq = G₁ + G₂ + ...
• Two Resistors in Parallel: R_eq = (R₁ R₂) / (R₁ + R₂)
• Current Divider Rule (CDR) for two branches:
I₁ = I_s · [ R₂ / (R₁ + R₂) ] | I₂ = I_s · [ R₁ / (R₁ + R₂) ]
Note: Current branches inversely proportional to resistances (CDR divides by opposite branch!).
Dynamic vs. Static Resistance in Non-Linear Devices
• Static (DC) Resistance: R_DC = V_Q / I_Q (Slope of chord from origin).
• Dynamic (AC / Incremental) Resistance: r_ac = dv / di |_Q
r_ac = 1 / (di/dv)|_Q (Reciprocal of tangent slope at Q)
• Tunnel Diodes / UJTs can exhibit Negative Incremental Resistance (r_ac < 0)!
• For bilateral elements: V-I curve is symmetric under 180° rotation about origin.
★ Bilateral: Resistor, Inductor, Capacitor. Non-bilateral: PN Diode, Transistor.
2. Ideal Inductor & Faraday Dynamics
Faraday-Lenz Law & Constitutive Equations
• Magnetic Flux Linkage: λ(t) = N Φ(t) = L · i(t)
• Terminal Voltage: v(t) = dλ/dt = L · (di/dt)
i(t) = i(t₀) + (1/L) ∫ v(τ) dτ from t₀ to t
• Physical unit: 1 Henry = 1 V·s / A = 1 Wb / A.
Stored Magnetic Energy:
★ Inductor Current Continuity Axiom
• For any finite terminal voltage v(t), the current CANNOT jump instantaneously:
i_L(0⁺) = i_L(0⁻) (State Variable Invariant)
Mathematical Proof via Contradiction:
If Δi = i(0⁺) - i(0⁻) ≠ 0 in Δt → 0, then di/dt → ∞,
v_L = L (di/dt) → ∞ (Requires infinite voltage / impulse δ(t)!).
• Without an explicit Dirac impulse voltage, current is strictly continuous.
Inductor Operating Regimes:
• At DC Steady-State (di/dt = 0): v_L = 0 V ⇒ IDEAL SHORT CIRCUIT!
• At Switching Instant t=0⁺ with i(0⁻)=0: ⇒ IDEAL OPEN CIRCUIT!
Series, Parallel & Mutual Inductance
• Series: L_eq = L₁ + L₂ + ... + L_n
• Parallel: 1/L_eq = 1/L₁ + 1/L₂ + ... (identical to resistors!)
Coupled Inductors & Dot Convention:
v₁ = L₁ (di₁/dt) ± M (di₂/dt) | v₂ = L₂ (di₂/dt) ± M (di₁/dt)
• Coupling Coefficient: k = M / √(L₁ L₂) where 0 ≤ k ≤ 1.
• Series-Aiding: L_eq = L₁ + L₂ + 2M
• Series-Opposing: L_eq = L₁ + L₂ - 2M
• Parallel-Aiding: L_eq = (L₁ L₂ - M²) / (L₁ + L₂ - 2M)
• Parallel-Opposing: L_eq = (L₁ L₂ - M²) / (L₁ + L₂ + 2M)
Frequency Domain & Impedance Behavior
• Phasor Impedance: Z_L(s) = sL ⇒ Z_L(jω) = jωL = ωL ∠+90°
• Current lags voltage by 90° in pure inductor (CIVIL mnemonic).
• As ω → 0 (DC): |Z_L| → 0 Ω (Short Circuit).
• As ω → ∞ (High Freq): |Z_L| → ∞ Ω (Open Circuit).
• Quality Factor of Real Inductor: Q = ωL / R_series.
• Choke Inductor: Passes DC, blocks high-frequency AC ripple.
3. Ideal Capacitor & Maxwell Dynamics
Constitutive V-I Relation & Displacement Current
• Charge Storage: q(t) = C · v(t)
• Displacement Current: i(t) = dq/dt = C · (dv/dt)
v(t) = v(t₀) + (1/C) ∫ i(τ) dτ from t₀ to t
• Physical unit: 1 Farad = 1 C / V = 1 A·s / V.
Stored Electrostatic Energy:
★ Capacitor Voltage Continuity Axiom
• For any finite branch current i(t), voltage CANNOT jump instantaneously:
v_C(0⁺) = v_C(0⁻) (State Variable Invariant)
Mathematical Proof via Contradiction:
If Δv = v(0⁺) - v(0⁻) ≠ 0 in Δt → 0, then dv/dt → ∞,
i_C = C (dv/dt) → ∞ (Requires infinite current impulse δ(t)!).
• Without an impulse current injection, voltage is strictly continuous.
Capacitor Operating Regimes:
• At DC Steady-State (dv/dt = 0): i_C = 0 A ⇒ IDEAL OPEN CIRCUIT!
• At Switching Instant t=0⁺ with v(0⁻)=0: ⇒ IDEAL SHORT CIRCUIT!
Series, Parallel & Duality Matrix
• Parallel (Common Voltage): C_eq = C₁ + C₂ + ... + C_n
• Series (Common Current): 1/C_eq = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ + ...
Two series capacitors: C_eq = (C₁ C₂) / (C₁ + C₂)
Master RLC Dualities:
Inductor (L) ⟷ Capacitor (C)
Current i(t) ⟷ Voltage v(t)
Flux λ(t) ⟷ Charge q(t)
Open Circuit (DC at t=0⁺) ⟷ Short Circuit (DC at t=0⁺)
Short Circuit (DC at t=∞) ⟷ Open Circuit (DC at t=∞)
Series L_eq = ∑ L_k ⟷ Parallel C_eq = ∑ C_k
Frequency Domain & Impedance Behavior
• Phasor Impedance: Z_C(s) = 1/(sC) ⇒ Z_C(jω) = 1/(jωC) = (1/ωC) ∠-90°
• Current leads voltage by 90° in pure capacitor (CIVIL mnemonic).
• As ω → 0 (DC): |Z_C| → ∞ Ω (Blocks DC completely!).
• As ω → ∞ (High Freq): |Z_C| → 0 Ω (Bypasses AC ripple to ground).
• Loss Tangent / ESR: tan δ = 1 / (ω C R_shunt) or ω C R_esr.
• DC Blocking / AC Coupling capacitor in analog amplifiers.
4. The 4 Dependent Source Topologies
1. VCVS (Voltage-Controlled Voltage Source)
• Output voltage governed by remote controlling voltage v_x:
v_s = μ · v_x (μ = Voltage Gain, Dimensionless [V/V])
• Symbol: Diamond with (+, -) polarities; label μ v_x.
• Physical Realization: Operational Amplifiers (Non-inverting / Inverting),
Thevenin equivalent of voltage feedback systems.
• Input Impedance: R_in → ∞ (Draws zero controlling current).
• Output Impedance: R_out → 0 (Maintains μ v_x regardless of load).
2. VCCS (Voltage-Controlled Current Source)
• Output current governed by remote controlling voltage v_x:
i_s = g_m · v_x (g_m = Transconductance [A/V or S])
• Symbol: Diamond with internal arrow; label g_m v_x.
• Physical Realization: MOSFET small-signal model (i_d = g_m v_gs),
BJT hybrid-pi model (i_c = g_m v_be), Operational Transconductance Amp (OTA).
• Input Impedance: R_in → ∞ | Output Impedance: R_out → ∞.
• S-domain / Admittance matrix: Enters mutual admittance terms.
3. CCVS (Current-Controlled Voltage Source)
• Output voltage governed by remote controlling current i_x:
v_s = r_m · i_x (r_m = Transresistance [V/A or Ω])
• Symbol: Diamond with (+, -) polarities; label r_m i_x.
• Physical Realization: Transimpedance Amplifier (TIA, e.g. photodiode readout),
coupled inductor z-parameter representation.
• Input Impedance: R_in → 0 | Output Impedance: R_out → 0.
• Controlling current i_x flows through a closed branch or short circuit.
4. CCCS (Current-Controlled Current Source)
• Output current governed by remote controlling current i_x:
i_s = β · i_x (β = Current Gain, Dimensionless [A/A])
• Symbol: Diamond with internal arrow; label β i_x.
• Physical Realization: Bipolar Junction Transistor common-emitter (i_c = β i_b = h_fe i_b),
Current mirrors, Current conveyors.
• Input Impedance: R_in → 0 | Output Impedance: R_out → ∞.
★ Critical Exam Laws for Dependent Sources
1. Superposition Law: Dependent sources CANNOT be deactivated/zeroed!
2. Source Transformation: Fully valid for dependent sources AS LONG AS
the controlling variable (v_x or i_x) is outside the transformed branch!
3. Active / Passive Nature: Can absorb OR deliver power depending on circuit!
